Consider the following system of linear equations: {x+2y=0−3x−y+5z=0−2x−4y+z=0 Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

a
⟨−1,0,0⟩
b
⟨0,0,1⟩
c
⟨1,0,0⟩
d
⟨0,0,0⟩
e
⟨0,1,0⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[1200−3−150−2−410].

Transforming M to reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[1200−3−150−2−410]R2:=R2+3R1∼[12000550−2−410]R3:=R3+2R1∼[120005500010]R2:=15R2∼[120001100010]R2:=R2+(−1)R3∼[120001000010]R2:=R1+(−2)R2∼[100001000010].

The corresponding system is now
{x=0y=0z=0.

So, we have the solution x=0, y=0 and z=0. Or, in vector form ⟨0,0,0⟩.

question.name: Question 7
question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x+2z=3 \\  & -2x+y-3z=-4 \\  & 4x-3y+6z=-8\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 & -4 \\ 4 & -3 & 6 & -8\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 & -4 \\ 4 & -3 & 6 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 4 & -3 & 6 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & -20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 16 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 31 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 16 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -14\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x=31 \\  & y=16 \\  & z=-14.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the solution $x=31$, $y=16$ and $z=-14.$ Or, in vector form $⟨31,16,-14⟩.$

last_observation.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 & -4 \\ 4 & -3 & 6 & -8\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 & -4 \\ 4 & -3 & 6 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 4 & -3 & 6 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & -20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 16 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 31 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 16 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -14\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x=31 \\  & y=16 \\  & z=-14.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the solution $x=31$, $y=16$ and $z=-14.$ Or, in vector form $⟨31,16,-14⟩.$

question.name: Question 7
question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x+2z=3 \\  & -2x+y-3z=-4 \\  & 4x-3y+6z=-8\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 & -4 \\ 4 & -3 & 6 & -8\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 & -4 \\ 4 & -3 & 6 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 4 & -3 & 6 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & -20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 16 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 31 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 16 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -14\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x=31 \\  & y=16 \\  & z=-14.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the solution $x=31$, $y=16$ and $z=-14.$ Or, in vector form $⟨31,16,-14⟩.$

Consider the following system of linear equations: {x+2z=3−2x+y−3z=−44x−3y+6z=−8 Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

a
⟨−31,16,−14⟩

⟨31,−16,14⟩

⟨−31,−16,14⟩

⟨31,16,14⟩

⟨31,16,−14⟩

EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[1023−21−3−44−36−8].

Transforming M to reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[1023−21−3−44−36−8]R2:=R2+2R1∼[102301124−36−8]R3:=R3+(−4)R1∼[102301120−3−2−20]R3:=R3+3R2∼[10230112001−14]R2:=R2+(−1)R3∼[102301016001−14]R1:=R1+(−2)R3∼[1003101016001−14].

The corresponding system is now
{x=31y=16z=−14.

So, we have the solution x=31, y=16 and z=−14. Or, in vector form ⟨31,16,−14⟩.
question.knowledge_point: Finding the Reduced Row Echelon Form of a 3x3 System That Is Not in Row Echelon Form

solution.reasoning: Apply R_2←R_2+2R_1 and R_3←R_3−4R_1 to obtain [0,1,1 | 2] and [0,−3,−2 | −20]. Then R_3←R_3+3R_2 gives z=−14. Applying R_2←R_2−R_3 and R_1←R_1−2R_3 gives the RREF [I | (31,16,−14)^T]. Thus choice e is mathematically correct. No MA answer or grade for this question is captured; the worked example concerns a different system.

question.name: Question 8
question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x-y+2z=5 \\  & 2x-y+7z=7 \\  & x-y+3z=5\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 5 \\ 2 & -1 & 7 & 7 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 5 \\ 2 & -1 & 7 & 7 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}-2{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x=2 \\  & y=-3 \\  & z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the solution $x=2$, $y=-3$, and $z=0.$ Or, in vector form, $⟨2,-3,0⟩.$

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 5 \\ 2 & -1 & 7 & 7 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}].

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 5 \\ 2 & -1 & 7 & 7 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}-2{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x=2 \\  & y=-3 \\  & z=0.\end{aligned}

question.name: Question 8
question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x-y+2z=5 \\  & 2x-y+7z=7 \\  & x-y+3z=5\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 5 \\ 2 & -1 & 7 & 7 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}].

\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 5 \\ 2 & -1 & 7 & 7 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}-2{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x=2 \\  & y=-3 \\  & z=0.\end{aligned}

Question 8
?

Consider the following system of linear equations: {x−y+2z=52x−y+7z=7x−y+3z=5 Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

a
⟨3,−2,0⟩
b
⟨2,−3,1⟩
c
⟨2,−3,0⟩
d
⟨−2,3,0⟩
e
⟨−2,3,−1⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is

M=[1−1252−1771−135].

Transforming M to reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[1−1252−1771−135]R2:=R2−2R1∼[1−125013−31−135]R3:=R3−R1∼[1−125013−30010]R2:=R2−3R3∼[1−125010−30010]R1:=R1−2R3∼[1−105010−30010]R1:=R1+R2∼[1002010−30010].

The corresponding system is now {x=2y=−3z=0.

So, we have the solution x=2, y=−3, and z=0. Or, in vector form, ⟨2,−3,0⟩.

solution.reasoning: Apply R_2←R_2−2R_1 and R_3←R_3−R_1 to obtain [0,1,3 | −3] and [0,0,1 | 0]. Then apply R_2←R_2−3R_3, R_1←R_1−2R_3, and R_1←R_1+R_2. The RREF is [I | (2,−3,0)^T], giving choice c. Question 8
?

Consider the following system of linear equations: {x−y+2z=52x−y+7z=7x−y+3z=5 Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

a
⟨3,−2,0⟩
b
⟨2,−3,1⟩
c
⟨2,−3,0⟩
d
⟨−2,3,0⟩
e
⟨−2,3,−1⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is

M=[1−1252−1771−135].

Transforming M to reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[1−1252−1771−135]R2:=R2−2R1∼[1−125013−31−135]R3:=R3−R1∼[1−125013−30010]R2:=R2−3R3∼[1−125010−30010]R1:=R1−2R3∼[1−105010−30010]R1:=R1+R2∼[1002010−30010].

The corresponding system is now {x=2y=−3z=0.

So, we have the solution x=2, y=−3, and z=0. Or, in vector form, ⟨2,−3,0⟩.

question.name: Question 9
question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x-y+z=1 \\  & 2x-y+z=3 \\  & -x+y=-3\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.

question.name: Question 9
question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x-y+z=1 \\  & 2x-y+z=3 \\  & -x+y=-3\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.

question.html:
Question 9
?

Consider the following system of linear equations: {x−y+z=12x−y+z=3−x+y=−3 Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form.

a
M∼[100−2010−1001−2]
b
M∼[100−20103001−2]
c
M∼[10020101001−2]
d
M∼[1002010−1001−2]
e
M∼[1002010−10012]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[1−1112−113−110−3].

Transforming M to reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[1−1112−113−110−3]R2:=R2−2R1∼[1−11101−11−110−3]R3:=R3+R1∼[1−11101−11001−2]R2:=R2+R3∼[1−111010−1001−2]R1:=R1−R3∼[1−103010−1001−2]R1:=R1+R2∼[1002010−1001−2]
question.knowledge_point: Finding the Reduced Row Echelon Form of a 3x3 System That Is Not in Row Echelon Form

solution.reasoning: Apply R_2←R_2−2R_1 and R_3←R_3+R_1 to obtain [0,1,−1 | 1] and [0,0,1 | −2]. Then R_2←R_2+R_3, R_1←R_1−R_3, and R_1←R_1+R_2 produce [I | (2,−1,−2)^T], matching choice d. No MA answer or grade for this question is captured; the worked example concerns a different system.

feedback.name: Question 9
feedback.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x-y+z=1 \\  & 2x-y+z=3 \\  & -x+y=-3\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.

question.name: Question 10
question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x-2y+z=8 \\  & 2x-3y+2z=14 \\  & 3x-6y+2z=21\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 8 \\ 2 & -3 & 2 & 14 \\ 3 & -6 & 2 & 21\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 8 \\ 2 & -3 & 2 & 14 \\ 3 & -6 & 2 & 21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 3 & -6 & 2 & 21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=(-1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+2{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x=1 \\  & y=-2 \\  & z=3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the solution $x=1$, $y=-2$ and $z=3.$ Or, in vector form $⟨1,-2,3⟩.$

last_observation.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 8 \\ 2 & -3 & 2 & 14 \\ 3 & -6 & 2 & 21\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 8 \\ 2 & -3 & 2 & 14 \\ 3 & -6 & 2 & 21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 3 & -6 & 2 & 21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=(-1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+2{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x=1 \\  & y=-2 \\  & z=3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the solution $x=1$, $y=-2$ and $z=3.$ Or, in vector form $⟨1,-2,3⟩.$

question.name: Question 10
question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x-2y+z=8 \\  & 2x-3y+2z=14 \\  & 3x-6y+2z=21\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

Consider the following system of linear equations: {x−2y+z=82x−3y+2z=143x−6y+2z=21 Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

a
⟨1,0,3⟩
b
⟨1,−2,3⟩
c
⟨1,−2,−3⟩

⟨1,2,3⟩

⟨−1,−2,3⟩
Submit
Correct

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[1−2182−32143−6221].

Transforming M to reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[1−2182−32143−6221]R2:=R2+(−2)R1∼[1−218010−23−6221]R3:=R3+(−3)R1∼[1−218010−200−1−3]R3:=(−1)R3∼[1−218010−20013]R1:=R1+(−1)R3∼[1−205010−20013]R1:=R1+2R3∼[1001010−20013].

The corresponding system is now
{x=1y=−2z=3.

So, we have the solution x=1, y=−2 and z=3. Or, in vector form ⟨1,−2,3⟩.

solution.reasoning: Apply R_2←R_2−2R_1 and R_3←R_3−3R_1 to obtain [0,1,0 | −2] and [0,0,−1 | −3]. Then R_3←−R_3, R_1←R_1−R_3, and R_1←R_1+2R_2 give the RREF [I | (1,−2,3)^T]. Thus choice b is mathematically correct. No MA answer or grade for this question is captured; the supplied worked example concerns a different system.

question.name: Question 11
question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4x-11y+5z=-1 \\ x-3y+2z=1 \\ -3x+9y-6z=-3\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}4 & -11 & 5 & -1 \\ 1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ -3 & 9 & -6 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & -11 & 5 & -1 \\ 1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ -3 & 9 & -6 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 4 & -11 & 5 & -1 \\ -3 & 9 & -6 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -5 \\ -3 & 9 & -6 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -7 & -14 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

Consider the following system of linear equations: {4x−11y+5z=−1x−3y+2z=1−3x+9y−6z=−3 Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form.

a
[100−14010−5001−1]
b
[10−7−1401−3−5001−1]
c
[1011−14013−50000]
d
[10−7−1401−3−50000]
e
[1011−1401−3−50000]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[4−115−11−321−39−6−3].

Transforming M to reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[4−115−11−321−39−6−3]R1↔R2∼[1−3214−115−1−39−6−3]R2:=R2+(−4)R1∼[1−32101−3−5−39−6−3]R3:=R3+3R1∼[1−32101−3−50000].

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the 1st and 2nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

M∼[1−32101−3−50000]R1:=R1+3R2∼[10−7−1401−3−50000].

last_observation.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}4 & -11 & 5 & -1 \\ 1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ -3 & 9 & -6 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & -11 & 5 & -1 \\ 1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ -3 & 9 & -6 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 4 & -11 & 5 & -1 \\ -3 & 9 & -6 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -5 \\ -3 & 9 & -6 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -7 & -14 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 11
question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4x-11y+5z=-1 \\ x-3y+2z=1 \\ -3x+9y-6z=-3\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & -11 & 5 & -1 \\ 1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ -3 & 9 & -6 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 4 & -11 & 5 & -1 \\ -3 & 9 & -6 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -5 \\ -3 & 9 & -6 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -7 & -14 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 11
?

Consider the following system of linear equations: {4x−11y+5z=−1x−3y+2z=1−3x+9y−6z=−3 Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form.

a
[100−14010−5001−1]
b
[10−7−1401−3−5001−1]
c
[1011−14013−50000]
d
[10−7−1401−3−50000]
e
[1011−1401−3−50000]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[4−115−11−321−39−6−3].

Transforming M to reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[4−115−11−321−39−6−3]R1↔R2∼[1−3214−115−1−39−6−3]R2:=R2+(−4)R1∼[1−32101−3−5−39−6−3]R3:=R3+3R1∼[1−32101−3−50000].

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the 1st and 2nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

M∼[1−32101−3−50000]R1:=R1+3R2∼[10−7−1401−3−50000].
question.knowledge_point: Finding the Reduced Row Echelon Form of a Singular 3x3 System With Two Pivots

solution.reasoning: Swap R_1 and R_2. Then R_2←R_2−4R_1 gives [0,1,−3 | −5], and R_3←R_3+3R_1 gives a zero row. Finally, R_1←R_1+3R_2 gives [1,0,−7 | −14]. This RREF matches choice d. No MA answer or grade for this question is captured; the worked example concerns a different system.

feedback.name: Question 11
feedback.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4x-11y+5z=-1 \\ x-3y+2z=1 \\ -3x+9y-6z=-3\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
feedback.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}4 & -11 & 5 & -1 \\ 1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ -3 & 9 & -6 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & -11 & 5 & -1 \\ 1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ -3 & 9 & -6 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 4 & -11 & 5 & -1 \\ -3 & 9 & -6 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -5 \\ -3 & 9 & -6 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -7 & -14 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 12
question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x-5y+5z=-1 \\ -2x+10y=-4 \\ x-5y=2\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & 5 & -1 \\ -2 & 10 & 0 & -4 \\ 1 & -5 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ into reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & 5 & -1 \\ -2 & 10 & 0 & -4 \\ 1 & -5 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 & 2 \\ -2 & 10 & 0 & -4 \\ 2 & -5 & 5 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & 5 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 5 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & 5 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+5{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 5 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+5z=-3 \\ y+z=-1 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final equation, we can remove this equation from the system. 

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=-3-5z \\ y=-z-1 \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3-5z \\ -z-1 \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

Consider the following system of linear equations: {2x−5y+5z=−1−2x+10y=−4x−5y=2 Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

a
[−3−5z−z−1z],z∈(−∞,∞)
b
[3−5zz−1z+5],z∈(−∞,∞)
c
[5z−3z+1z−5],z∈(−∞,∞)
d
[3−5zz−1z],z∈(−∞,∞)
e
[5z−3−z−1z],z∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[2−55−1−2100−41−502].

Transforming M into reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[2−55−1−2100−41−502]R1↔R3∼[1−502−2100−42−55−1]R2:=R2+2R1∼[1−50200002−55−1]R3:=R3+(−2)R1∼[1−5020000055−5]R2↔R3∼[1−502055−50000]R3:=15R3∼[1−502011−10000].

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the 1st and 2nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

M∼[1−502011−10000]R1:=R1+5R2∼[105−3011−10000].

The corresponding system is now {x+5z=−3y+z=−10=0.

Since any numbers x,y,z form a solution of the final equation, we can remove this equation from the system.

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are x and y, and we have one free variable, z. That means we need to find x and y in terms of z.

Therefore, the general solution is

{x=−3−5zy=−z−1z=z,

where z (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as [xyz]=[−3−5z−z−1z],z∈(−∞,∞).

last_observation.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & 5 & -1 \\ -2 & 10 & 0 & -4 \\ 1 & -5 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ into reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & 5 & -1 \\ -2 & 10 & 0 & -4 \\ 1 & -5 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 & 2 \\ -2 & 10 & 0 & -4 \\ 2 & -5 & 5 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & 5 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 5 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & 5 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+5{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 5 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+5z=-3 \\ y+z=-1 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final equation, we can remove this equation from the system. 

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=-3-5z \\ y=-z-1 \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3-5z \\ -z-1 \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

a
[−3−5z−z−1z],z∈(−∞,∞)
b

c

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[2−55−1−2100−41−502].

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the 1st and 2nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

M∼[1−502011−10000]R1:=R1+5R2∼[105−3011−10000].

The corresponding system is now {x+5z=−3y+z=−10=0.

Since any numbers x,y,z form a solution of the final equation, we can remove this equation from the system.

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are x and y, and we have one free variable, z. That means we need to find x and y in terms of z.

Therefore, the general solution is

{x=−3−5zy=−z−1z=z,

where z (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as [xyz]=[−3−5z−z−1z],z∈(−∞,∞).
question.knowledge_point: Finding the Reduced Row Echelon Form of a Singular 3x3 System With Two Pivots

solution.reasoning: Swap R_1 and R_3. Apply R_2←R_2+2R_1 and R_3←R_3−2R_1, obtaining a zero row and [0,5,5 | −5]. Move the zero row to the bottom, divide the second row by 5, and apply R_1←R_1+5R_2. The RREF has rows [1,0,5 | −3], [0,1,1 | −1], and [0,0,0 | 0]. Thus x=−3−5z and y=−z−1, with z arbitrary, matching choice a. No MA answer or grade for this question is captured; the worked example concerns a different system.

feedback.name: Question 12
feedback.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x-5y+5z=-1 \\ -2x+10y=-4 \\ x-5y=2\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
feedback.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & 5 & -1 \\ -2 & 10 & 0 & -4 \\ 1 & -5 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ into reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & 5 & -1 \\ -2 & 10 & 0 & -4 \\ 1 & -5 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 & 2 \\ -2 & 10 & 0 & -4 \\ 2 & -5 & 5 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & 5 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 5 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & 5 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+5{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 5 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+5z=-3 \\ y+z=-1 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final equation, we can remove this equation from the system. 

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=-3-5z \\ y=-z-1 \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3-5z \\ -z-1 \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

a

b

c

EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[2−55−1−2100−41−502].

Transforming M into reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[2−55−1−2100−41−502]R1↔R3∼[1−502−2100−42−55−1]R2:=R2+2R1∼[1−50200002−55−1]R3:=R3+(−2)R1∼[1−5020000055−5]R2↔R3∼[1−502055−50000]R3:=15R3∼[1−502011−10000].

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the 1st and 2nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

M∼[1−502011−10000]R1:=R1+5R2∼[105−3011−10000].

The corresponding system is now {x+5z=−3y+z=−10=0.

Since any numbers x,y,z form a solution of the final equation, we can remove this equation from the system.

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are x and y, and we have one free variable, z. That means we need to find x and y in terms of z.

Therefore, the general solution is

{x=−3−5zy=−z−1z=z,

where z (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as [xyz]=[−3−5z−z−1z],z∈(−∞,∞).

question.name: Question 13
question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-y+z=3 \\ x+2y-2z=0 \\ -2x+2y-2z=-6\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & -2 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & -2 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -3 \\ -2 & 2 & -2 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 13
?

Consider the following system of linear equations: {x−y+z=3x+2y−2z=0−2x+2y−2z=−6 Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form.

a
[1002010−10010]
b
[100201−1−10000]
c
[100201110000]
d
[100201−1−10010]
e
[1002010−10000]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[1−11312−20−22−2−6].

Transforming M to reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[1−11312−20−22−2−6]R2:=R2+(−1)R1∼[1−11303−3−3−22−2−6]R3:=R3+2R1∼[1−11303−3−30000]R2:=13R2∼[1−11301−1−10000].

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the 1st and 2nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

M∼[1−11301−1−10000]R1:=R1+R2∼[100201−1−10000].

last_observation.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & -2 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & -2 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -3 \\ -2 & 2 & -2 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 13
question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-y+z=3 \\ x+2y-2z=0 \\ -2x+2y-2z=-6\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.

Question 13
?

Consider the following system of linear equations: {x−y+z=3x+2y−2z=0−2x+2y−2z=−6 Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form.

a
[1002010−10010]
b
[100201−1−10000]
c
[100201110000]
d
[100201−1−10010]
e
[1002010−10000]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[1−11312−20−22−2−6].

Transforming M to reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[1−11312−20−22−2−6]R2:=R2+(−1)R1∼[1−11303−3−3−22−2−6]R3:=R3+2R1∼[1−11303−3−30000]R2:=13R2∼[1−11301−1−10000].

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the 1st and 2nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

M∼[1−11301−1−10000]R1:=R1+R2∼[100201−1−10000].
question.knowledge_point: Finding the Reduced Row Echelon Form of a Singular 3x3 System With Two Pivots

solution.reasoning: Apply R_2←R_2−R_1 and R_3←R_3+2R_1 to obtain [0,3,−3 | −3] and a zero row. Divide R_2 by 3, then apply R_1←R_1+R_2. The resulting rows are [1,0,0 | 2], [0,1,−1 | −1], and [0,0,0 | 0], matching choice b. No MA answer or grade for this question is captured; the worked example concerns a different system.

feedback.name: Question 13
feedback.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-y+z=3 \\ x+2y-2z=0 \\ -2x+2y-2z=-6\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
feedback.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & -2 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & -2 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -3 \\ -2 & 2 & -2 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 14
question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+2y-3z=1 \\ 3x+8y-z=-1 \\ 2x+4y-6z=2\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 3 & 8 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & 4 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 3 & 8 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & 4 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 8 & -4 \\ 2 & 4 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 8 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -11 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

Consider the following system of linear equations: {x+2y−3z=13x+8y−z=−12x+4y−6z=2 Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form.

a
[10−115014−40000]
b
[10−53014−20000]
c
[10−115014−20000]
d
[10−113014−10000]
e
[10−55014−10000]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[12−3138−1−124−62].

Transforming M to reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[12−3138−1−124−62]R2:=R2−3R1∼[12−31028−424−62]R3:=R3−2R1∼[12−31028−40000]R2:=12R2∼[12−31014−20000].

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the 1st and 2nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

M∼[12−31014−20000]R1:=R1−2R2∼[10−115014−20000].

last_observation.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 3 & 8 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & 4 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 3 & 8 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & 4 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 8 & -4 \\ 2 & 4 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 8 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -11 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 14
question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+2y-3z=1 \\ 3x+8y-z=-1 \\ 2x+4y-6z=2\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.

Question 14
?

Consider the following system of linear equations: {x+2y−3z=13x+8y−z=−12x+4y−6z=2 Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form.

a
[10−115014−40000]
b
[10−53014−20000]
c
[10−115014−20000]
d
[10−113014−10000]
e
[10−55014−10000]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[12−3138−1−124−62].

Transforming M to reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[12−3138−1−124−62]R2:=R2−3R1∼[12−31028−424−62]R3:=R3−2R1∼[12−31028−40000]R2:=12R2∼[12−31014−20000].

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the 1st and 2nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

M∼[12−31014−20000]R1:=R1−2R2∼[10−115014−20000].
question.knowledge_point: Finding the Reduced Row Echelon Form of a Singular 3x3 System With Two Pivots

solution.reasoning: Apply R_2←R_2−3R_1 and R_3←R_3−2R_1 to obtain [0,2,8 | −4] and a zero row. Divide R_2 by 2, then apply R_1←R_1−2R_2. The RREF has rows [1,0,−11 | 5], [0,1,4 | −2], and [0,0,0 | 0], matching choice c. No MA answer or grade for this question is captured; the worked example concerns a different system.

feedback.name: Question 14
feedback.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+2y-3z=1 \\ 3x+8y-z=-1 \\ 2x+4y-6z=2\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
feedback.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 3 & 8 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & 4 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 3 & 8 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & 4 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 8 & -4 \\ 2 & 4 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 8 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -11 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[12−3138−1−124−62].

Transforming M to reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[12−3138−1−124−62]R2:=R2−3R1∼[12−31028−424−62]R3:=R3−2R1∼[12−31028−40000]R2:=12R2∼[12−31014−20000].

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the 1st and 2nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-3y-2z=-5 \\ -3x+5y+2z=3 \\ 3x-9y-6z=-15\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ -3 & 5 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & -9 & -6 & -15\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ into reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ -3 & 5 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & -9 & -6 & -15\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & -4 & -4 & -12 \\ 3 & -9 & -6 & -15\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & -4 & -4 & -12 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{4}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+z=4 \\ y+z=3 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final equation, we can remove this equation from the system. 

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=4-z \\ y=3-z \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4-z \\ 3-z \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

last_observation.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ -3 & 5 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & -9 & -6 & -15\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ into reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ -3 & 5 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & -9 & -6 & -15\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & -4 & -4 & -12 \\ 3 & -9 & -6 & -15\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & -4 & -4 & -12 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{4}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+z=4 \\ y+z=3 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final equation, we can remove this equation from the system. 

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=4-z \\ y=3-z \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4-z \\ 3-z \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-3y-2z=-5 \\ -3x+5y+2z=3 \\ 3x-9y-6z=-15\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[1−3−2−5−35233−9−6−15].

Transforming M into reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[1−3−2−5−35233−9−6−15]R2:=R2+3R1∼[1−3−2−50−4−4−123−9−6−15]R3:=R3−3R1∼[1−3−2−50−4−4−120000]R2:=−14R2∼[1−3−2−501130000]

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the 1st and 2nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

M∼[1−3−2−501130000]R1:=R1+3R2∼[101401130000].

The corresponding system is now {x+z=4y+z=30=0.

Since any numbers x,y,z form a solution of the final equation, we can remove this equation from the system.

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are x and y, and we have one free variable, z. That means we need to find x and y in terms of z.

Therefore, the general solution is

{x=4−zy=3−zz=z,

where z (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

question.knowledge_point: Finding the Reduced Row Echelon Form of a Singular 3x3 System With Two Pivots

solution.reasoning: Apply R_2←R_2+3R_1 and R_3←R_3−3R_1 to obtain [0,−4,−4 | −12] and a zero row. Divide R_2 by −4, then apply R_1←R_1+3R_2. The RREF has rows [1,0,1 | 4], [0,1,1 | 3], and [0,0,0 | 0]. Hence x=4−z and y=3−z, with z arbitrary, matching choice a. No MA answer or grade for this question is captured; the worked example concerns a different system.

feedback.name: Question 15
feedback.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-3y-2z=-5 \\ -3x+5y+2z=3 \\ 3x-9y-6z=-15\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
feedback.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ -3 & 5 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & -9 & -6 & -15\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ into reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ -3 & 5 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & -9 & -6 & -15\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & -4 & -4 & -12 \\ 3 & -9 & -6 & -15\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & -4 & -4 & -12 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{4}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+z=4 \\ y+z=3 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final equation, we can remove this equation from the system. 

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=4-z \\ y=3-z \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4-z \\ 3-z \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the following system of linear equations: {x−3y−2z=−5−3x+5y+2z=33x−9y−6z=−15 Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

a
[4−z3−zz],z∈(−∞,∞)
b
[z−4z−3z],z∈(−∞,∞)
c
[z+4z+3z],z∈(−∞,∞)
d
[zzz],z∈(−∞,∞)
e
No solution
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[1−3−2−5−35233−9−6−15].

Transforming M into reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[1−3−2−5−35233−9−6−15]R2:=R2+3R1∼[1−3−2−50−4−4−123−9−6−15]R3:=R3−3R1∼[1−3−2−50−4−4−120000]R2:=−14R2∼[1−3−2−501130000]

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the 1st and 2nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

M∼[1−3−2−501130000]R1:=R1+3R2∼[101401130000].

The corresponding system is now {x+z=4y+z=30=0.

Since any numbers x,y,z form a solution of the final equation, we can remove this equation from the system.

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are x and y, and we have one free variable, z. That means we need to find x and y in terms of z.

Therefore, the general solution is

{x=4−zy=3−zz=z,

where z (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as [xyz]=[4−z3−zz],z∈(−∞,∞).

question.name: Question 16
question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x+4y-6z=4 \\ 6x+12y-18z=12 \\ -10x-20y+30z=-20\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -6 & 4 \\ 6 & 12 & -18 & 12 \\ -10 & -20 & 30 & -20\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -6 & 4 \\ 6 & 12 & -18 & 12 \\ -10 & -20 & 30 & -20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 2 \\ 6 & 12 & -18 & 12 \\ -10 & -20 & 30 & -20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-6){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -10 & -20 & 30 & -20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+10{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 16
question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x+4y-6z=4 \\ 6x+12y-18z=12 \\ -10x-20y+30z=-20\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.

question.html:
Question 16
?

Consider the following system of linear equations: {2x+4y−6z=46x+12y−18z=12−10x−20y+30z=−20 Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form.

a
[12−3000020000]
b
[12−3200100000]
c
[12−6201000000]
d
[1002010−20016]
e
[12−3200000000]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[24−64612−1812−10−2030−20].

Transforming M to reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[24−64612−1812−10−2030−20]R1:=12R1∼[12−32612−1812−10−2030−20]R2:=R2+(−6)R1∼[12−320000−10−2030−20]R3:=R3+10R1∼[12−3200000000].
question.knowledge_point: Finding the Reduced Row Echelon Form of a Singular 3x3 System With One Pivot

solution.reasoning: Divide R_1 by 2 to obtain [1,2,−3 | 2]. Then apply R_2←R_2−6R_1 and R_3←R_3+10R_1; both become zero rows. This is reduced row echelon form and matches choice e. No MA answer or grade for this question is captured; the worked example concerns a different system.

feedback.name: Question 16
feedback.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x+4y-6z=4 \\ 6x+12y-18z=12 \\ -10x-20y+30z=-20\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
feedback.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -6 & 4 \\ 6 & 12 & -18 & 12 \\ -10 & -20 & 30 & -20\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -6 & 4 \\ 6 & 12 & -18 & 12 \\ -10 & -20 & 30 & -20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 2 \\ 6 & 12 & -18 & 12 \\ -10 & -20 & 30 & -20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-6){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -10 & -20 & 30 & -20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+10{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 17
question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x-4y-8z=4 \\ 3x-6y-12z=6 \\ -4x+8y+16z=-8\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & -8 & 4 \\ 3 & -6 & -12 & 6 \\ -4 & 8 & 16 & -8\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & -8 & 4 \\ 3 & -6 & -12 & 6 \\ -4 & 8 & 16 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -4 & 2 \\ 3 & -6 & -12 & 6 \\ -4 & 8 & 16 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 8 & 16 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 17
?

Consider the following system of linear equations: {2x−4y−8z=43x−6y−12z=6−4x+8y+16z=−8 Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form.

a
[124−200000000]
b
[1002011−10014]
c
[124200000000]
d
[1−2−4200000000]
e
[10−42011−10000]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[2−4−843−6−126−4816−8].

Transforming M to reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[2−4−843−6−126−4816−8]R1:=12R1∼[1−2−423−6−126−4816−8]R2:=R2−3R1∼[1−2−420000−4816−8]R3:=R3+4R1∼[1−2−4200000000].

question.name: Question 17
question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x-4y-8z=4 \\ 3x-6y-12z=6 \\ -4x+8y+16z=-8\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
question.worked_solution:

question.html:
Question 17
?

Consider the following system of linear equations: {2x−4y−8z=43x−6y−12z=6−4x+8y+16z=−8 Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form.

a
[124−200000000]
b
[1002011−10014]
c
[124200000000]
d
[1−2−4200000000]
e
[10−42011−10000]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[2−4−843−6−126−4816−8].

Transforming M to reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[2−4−843−6−126−4816−8]R1:=12R1∼[1−2−423−6−126−4816−8]R2:=R2−3R1∼[1−2−420000−4816−8]R3:=R3+4R1∼[1−2−4200000000].
question.knowledge_point: Finding the Reduced Row Echelon Form of a Singular 3x3 System With One Pivot

solution.reasoning: Divide R_1 by 2 to obtain [1,−2,−4 | 2]. Then apply R_2←R_2−3R_1 and R_3←R_3+4R_1; both become zero rows. The resulting RREF matches choice d. No MA answer or grade for this question is captured; the worked example concerns a different system.

feedback.name: Question 17
feedback.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x-4y-8z=4 \\ 3x-6y-12z=6 \\ -4x+8y+16z=-8\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
feedback.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & -8 & 4 \\ 3 & -6 & -12 & 6 \\ -4 & 8 & 16 & -8\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & -8 & 4 \\ 3 & -6 & -12 & 6 \\ -4 & 8 & 16 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -4 & 2 \\ 3 & -6 & -12 & 6 \\ -4 & 8 & 16 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 8 & 16 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 18
question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-3x-6y+15z=-3 \\ 6x+12y-30z=6 \\ -6x-12y+30z=-6\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -6 & 15 & -3 \\ 6 & 12 & -30 & 6 \\ -6 & -12 & 30 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & -6 & 15 & -3 \\ 6 & 12 & -30 & 6 \\ -6 & -12 & 30 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=(-\frac{1}{3}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -5 & 1 \\ 6 & 12 & -30 & 6 \\ -6 & -12 & 30 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-6){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -6 & -12 & 30 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+6{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+2y-5z=1 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final two equations, we can remove these equations from the system. 

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$, and we have two free variables, $y,$ and $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y$ and $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=1-2y+5z \\ y=y \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ and $z$ (the free variables) are arbitrary numbers.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1-2y+5z \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}],\,y,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 18
?

Consider the following system of linear equations: {−3x−6y+15z=−36x+12y−30z=6−6x−12y+30z=−6 Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

a
[−1+2y+zy−6z],y,z∈(−∞,∞)
b
[1−2y+5zyz],y,z∈(−∞,∞)
c
[1−2y−5zyz],y,z∈(−∞,∞)
d
[−1+2y+zyz],y,z∈(−∞,∞)
e
[1+2y−5z2yz],y,z∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[−3−615−3612−306−6−1230−6].

Transforming M to reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[−3−615−3612−306−6−1230−6]R1:=(−13)R1∼[12−51612−306−6−1230−6]R2:=R2+(−6)R1∼[12−510000−6−1230−6]R3:=R3+6R1∼[12−5100000000].

The corresponding system is now {x+2y−5z=10x+0y+0z=00x+0y+0z=0.

Since any numbers x,y,z form a solution of the final two equations, we can remove these equations from the system.

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is x, and we have two free variables, y, and z. That means we need to find x in terms of y and z.

Therefore, the general solution is

{x=1−2y+5zy=yz=z,

where y and z (the free variables) are arbitrary numbers.

In vector form, the solution can be written as [xyz]=[1−2y+5zyz],y,z∈(−∞,∞).

last_observation.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -6 & 15 & -3 \\ 6 & 12 & -30 & 6 \\ -6 & -12 & 30 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & -6 & 15 & -3 \\ 6 & 12 & -30 & 6 \\ -6 & -12 & 30 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=(-\frac{1}{3}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -5 & 1 \\ 6 & 12 & -30 & 6 \\ -6 & -12 & 30 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-6){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -6 & -12 & 30 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+6{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+2y-5z=1 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final two equations, we can remove these equations from the system. 

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$, and we have two free variables, $y,$ and $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y$ and $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=1-2y+5z \\ y=y \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ and $z$ (the free variables) are arbitrary numbers.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1-2y+5z \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}],\,y,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-3x-6y+15z=-3 \\ 6x+12y-30z=6 \\ -6x-12y+30z=-6\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

solution.reasoning: Divide R_1 by −3 to obtain [1,2,−5 | 1]. Then R_2←R_2−6R_1 and R_3←R_3+6R_1 produce two zero rows. Thus x+2y−5z=1, so x=1−2y+5z with y and z arbitrary, matching choice b. No MA answer or grade for this question is captured; the worked example concerns a different system.

feedback.name: Question 18
feedback.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-3x-6y+15z=-3 \\ 6x+12y-30z=6 \\ -6x-12y+30z=-6\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
feedback.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -6 & 15 & -3 \\ 6 & 12 & -30 & 6 \\ -6 & -12 & 30 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & -6 & 15 & -3 \\ 6 & 12 & -30 & 6 \\ -6 & -12 & 30 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=(-\frac{1}{3}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -5 & 1 \\ 6 & 12 & -30 & 6 \\ -6 & -12 & 30 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-6){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -6 & -12 & 30 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+6{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+2y-5z=1 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final two equations, we can remove these equations from the system. 

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$, and we have two free variables, $y,$ and $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y$ and $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=1-2y+5z \\ y=y \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ and $z$ (the free variables) are arbitrary numbers.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1-2y+5z \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}],\,y,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 19
question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-10y-5z=10 \\ -10x+100y+50z=-100 \\ -4x+40y+20z=-40\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -10 & -5 & 10 \\ -10 & 100 & 50 & -100 \\ -4 & 40 & 20 & -40\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -10 & -5 & 10 \\ -10 & 100 & 50 & -100 \\ -4 & 40 & 20 & -40\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+10{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -10 & -5 & 10 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 40 & 20 & -40\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -10 & -5 & 10 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 19
?

Consider the following system of linear equations: {x−10y−5z=10−10x+100y+50z=−100−4x+40y+20z=−40 Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form.

a
[10010010−100001−40]
b
[1−10−51000100000]
c
[1−10−510000−100000−40]
d
[1−10−51000000000]
e
[1−10−5000000000]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[1−10−510−1010050−100−44020−40].

Transforming M to reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[1−10−510−1010050−100−44020−40]R2:=R2+10R1∼[1−10−5100000−44020−40]R3:=R3+4R1∼[1−10−51000000000].

question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-10y-5z=10 \\ -10x+100y+50z=-100 \\ -4x+40y+20z=-40\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -10 & -5 & 10 \\ -10 & 100 & 50 & -100 \\ -4 & 40 & 20 & -40\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$

$$

question.html:
Question 19
?

Consider the following system of linear equations: {x−10y−5z=10−10x+100y+50z=−100−4x+40y+20z=−40 Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form.

a
[10010010−100001−40]
b
[1−10−51000100000]
c
[1−10−510000−100000−40]
d
[1−10−51000000000]
e
[1−10−5000000000]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[1−10−510−1010050−100−44020−40].

Transforming M to reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[1−10−510−1010050−100−44020−40]R2:=R2+10R1∼[1−10−5100000−44020−40]R3:=R3+4R1∼[1−10−51000000000].
question.knowledge_point: Finding the Reduced Row Echelon Form of a Singular 3x3 System With One Pivot

solution.reasoning: Apply R_2←R_2+10R_1 and R_3←R_3+4R_1. Both become zero rows, leaving [1,−10,−5 | 10] as the only nonzero row. This is reduced row echelon form and matches choice d. No MA answer or grade for this question is captured; the worked example concerns a different system.

feedback.name: Question 19
feedback.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-10y-5z=10 \\ -10x+100y+50z=-100 \\ -4x+40y+20z=-40\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
feedback.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -10 & -5 & 10 \\ -10 & 100 & 50 & -100 \\ -4 & 40 & 20 & -40\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -10 & -5 & 10 \\ -10 & 100 & 50 & -100 \\ -4 & 40 & 20 & -40\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+10{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -10 & -5 & 10 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 40 & 20 & -40\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -10 & -5 & 10 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 20
question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4x-8y+12z=-8 \\ x-2y+3z=-2 \\ -2x+4y-6z=4\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}4 & -8 & 12 & -8 \\ 1 & -2 & 3 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & -8 & 12 & -8 \\ 1 & -2 & 3 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 & -2 \\ 4 & -8 & 12 & -8 \\ -2 & 4 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-2y+3z=-2 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final two equations, we can remove these equations from the system. 

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$, and we have two free variables, $y,$ and $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y$ and $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=2y-3z-2 \\ y=y \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ and $z$ (the free variables) are arbitrary numbers.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2y-3z-2 \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}],\,y,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}

Question 20
?

Consider the following system of linear equations: {4x−8y+12z=−8x−2y+3z=−2−2x+4y−6z=4 Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

a
[2y+3z+2yz],y,z∈(−∞,∞)
b
No solution
c
[y−2z−1yz],y,z∈(−∞,∞)
d
[2−2y+3zyz],y,z∈(−∞,∞)
e
[2y−3z−2yz],y,z∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[4−812−81−23−2−24−64].

Transforming M to reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[4−812−81−23−2−24−64]R1↔R2∼[1−23−24−812−8−24−64]R2:=R2−4R1∼[1−23−20000−24−64]R3:=R3+2R1∼[1−23−200000000].

The corresponding system is now {x−2y+3z=−20x+0y+0z=00x+0y+0z=0.

Since any numbers x,y,z form a solution of the final two equations, we can remove these equations from the system.

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is x, and we have two free variables, y, and z. That means we need to find x in terms of y and z.

Therefore, the general solution is

{x=2y−3z−2y=yz=z,

where y and z (the free variables) are arbitrary numbers.

In vector form, the solution can be written as [xyz]=[2y−3z−2yz],y,z∈(−∞,∞).
